200.description:
The World of Warcraft: Forever builds people plan most on Talents Forever for one class, optionally one spec: the top level 60 build families and the most set 21-point builds at the level 30 beta cap, each with its points per tree, key talents, share and counts and a calculator link, plus the class's spec split and each spec's first 21 points from the leveling orders. Counts are the site's own tally, not a tier list.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attribution` | string | Credit line for the counts: Talents Forever's own tally, not a tier list. |
| `class` | string |  |
| `counted_on` | string | Day the counts were taken (`9 Oct 2026`). |
| `level_30` | object[] | The 21-point builds set most at level 30, the beta cap; empty when no family has reached the site's floor. |
| `level_30_from_leveling` | object[] | Each spec's first 21 points as its leading leveling order places them. |
| `level_60` | object[] | The most popular level 60 build families (46 or more of 51 points), best ranked first. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix time in milliseconds when this program read the source. |
| `spec` | string | Tree the rows were filtered to; null for every tree. |
| `spec_shares` | object[] | Share of the class's counted builds or orders that lead in each tree, as the page splits them. |
| `url` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

Spec slug of that class, to keep only builds or orders that lead in that tree: druid balance/feral/restoration, hunter beast-mastery/marksmanship/survival, mage arcane/fire/frost, paladin holy/protection/retribution, priest discipline/holy/shadow, rogue assassination/combat/subtlety, shaman elemental/enhancement/restoration, warlock affliction/demonology/destruction, warrior arms/fury/protection.

value.attribution: Counts from Talents Forever (https://talentsforever.com/), the site's own tally of builds planned on it. A count of what people plan, not a tier list.

brackets.holders: 1,722 of the 16,848 Arms builds that reach level 19 hold these points, 10.2%.
brackets.note: Across all 16,848 of those builds the talents taken most in these levels are Improved Rend (83%), Improved Tactical Mastery (65%), Deflection (49%) and Improved Heroic Strike (46%).

brackets.holders: 537 of the 4,294 Arms builds that reach level 29 hold these points, 12.5%.
brackets.note: Across all 4,294 of those builds the talents taken most in these levels are Deep Wounds (94%), Improved Overpower (81%), Anger Management (78%) and Impale (73%).

Fewer than 25 of the builds that follow the order above reach these levels the same way, so the order stops here rather than guess. Of the 1,015 that reach them, most put points in Sweeping Strikes (86%), Weaponmaster (79%), Two-Handed Weapon Specialization (76%) and Bloodthrill (67%).

orders.summary: The order runs to level 29: Improved Rend ×3, Deflection ×2, Improved Tactical Mastery ×5, Improved Overpower ×2, Deep Wounds ×3, Anger Management, Impale ×2, Two-Handed Weapon Specialization ×2.

200.description:
Every talent of one World of Warcraft: Forever class: the three trees with each talent's grid position, rank count, prerequisite, ability cost, the text of every rank and how it compares with Classic, plus the Classic talents Forever removed. With `build` (a Talents Forever calculator link), also the ranks that build puts in each talent and its points per tree. Data is CC BY 4.0: credit Talents Forever with the returned `attribution`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attribution` | string | Credit line to show with the data, as the licence asks. |
| `build` | object | The decoded build link; null without `build`. |
| `class` | string |  |
| `data_build` | string | Beta client build the trees were read from (`1.60.1.70291`). |
| `generated` | string | Date the export was generated (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `license` | string | Licence of the talent data: CC BY 4.0. |
| `license_url` | string |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix time in milliseconds when this program read the source. |
| `trees` | object[] | The three talent trees in the game's order. |
| `url` | string | The export read. |
